card.name: Verbs describing what a law requires
card.fires_on: Verbs and small linking words right after a law or its subject, such as 'prohibits', 'disallows', 'are', 'must', 'to', in web text about statutes and legal duties. It marks the spot where the text says what the law requires or bans.

modes.label: Law-describing verbs
modes.description: Verbs like prohibits or disallows right after an act of law is named.
modes.example: Age Discrimination in Employment Act of 1967 Considered to be among the landmark, Federal discrimination laws, it<< prohibits>> age discrimination in any aspect of employment against

modes.label: Duty words after who is covered
modes.description: Small words after the covered party, such as schools, colleges or employers, leading into what they must do.
modes.example: Under IDEA, schools<< are>> responsible to purchase AT if the need is

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words about legality and law, such as legally, legal and legality.
card.plain: It fires where a sentence is about to say what a law requires or forbids.
